planting.note: Set divisions just below the soil surface in spring after the threat of hard frost has passed.

directions: 'Big Smile' is a selection of the Chinese ground orchid prized for unusually large, pale blush-pink flowers with a cheerful yellow-flushed throat that opens wider than the species type. Pleated green leaves emerge in spring alongside slender flower spikes that bloom over several weeks. It thrives in part shade in loose, fertile, moisture-retentive soil, much like a woodland hosta companion. Established clumps bulk up steadily and can be lifted and divided in early spring for propagation.

planting.note: Plant pseudobulbs at the soil surface in spring in a sharply drained, shaded trough or raised bed.

directions: This pure white-flowered form of the Taiwan mountain orchid lacks the pink flush of the typical species, showing only faint yellow marking in the throat of its fringed lip against snowy petals. It blooms on bare stems in spring before the single pleated leaf unfurls, making a striking contrast with darker companions in a shaded alpine trough. Culture matches the species: a gritty, well-drained, humus-rich mix, high dappled shade, and protection from winter wet and hard freezes. Pseudobulbs multiply yearly and can be divided and repotted in early spring.

planting.note: Plant pseudobulbs shallowly in spring in a gritty, sharply drained, shaded bed.

directions: Collected from high, exposed mountain slopes in Sichuan and Yunnan, this compact species is regarded as one of the hardiest members of its genus and can survive outdoors through winter in a sheltered scree bed where many other Pleione need glasshouse protection. Bright magenta-pink flowers with a fringed, spotted lip open on short stems in spring just ahead of the single narrow leaf. Culture follows the usual Pleione pattern: fast-draining, humus-rich grit, dappled shade, summer moisture, and a dry winter rest to mimic its native dormancy. Pseudobulbs multiply into tight clusters that are easily separated in early spring.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in consistently moist, partly shaded soil near a water feature.

directions: This dark-foliaged selection of the native giant stream orchid was found growing on serpentine-derived soils and is grown for its blackish-purple-flushed stems and leaves, which contrast strikingly with the dusky maroon-green flowers typical of the species. Like the species, it wants a boggy or consistently moist, partly shaded position such as a pond or seep margin, where it spreads gradually by rhizome into a colony. Flowering occurs on arching racemes in late spring to early summer, with the hinged lip of each bloom moving slightly in the breeze. Divide crowded colonies in early spring, keeping divisions moist until re-established.
